task.description: REQ-232: retire parity-justification phrasing ('matches R-Co'/'mirrors R-Co'/'same as R-Co'/"R-Co's own"/'R-Co own'/'parity'/'port of R-Co') from comments and moduledocs across all 12 files in lib/letflow/routers/. Per occurrence, either restated the surrounding sentence on Letflow's own technical merit (the real invariant/contract/reason) or deleted the lineage framing where the code was self-evident without it, per ISS-0424's judgement-call criteria. Several edits initially over-deleted a .zig citation that shared a sentence with a lineage-justification phrase (instances.ex, identity.ex, tenants.ex, tasks.ex, promotions.ex, solution_packs.ex, definitions.ex, audit.ex all had at least one over-deletion on the first pass); all were caught by this exact grep check and every lost citation was restored, folded into the rewritten sentence, before finalizing.

technical_reasons_named_examples: instances.ex route-ordering paragraph: kept 'Plug.Router matches in declaration order, so a post "/:id" declared above these three would swallow all of them' as the real reason for the route order, not R-Co's registration order -- the R-Co citation (main.zig:848) is now parenthetical supporting evidence, not the justification.

definitions.ex DELETE handler: reframed the non-atomic get-then-act status check as 'an existing race in the underlying status model, not one this router introduces' -- the merit is that this router adds no new concurrency defect, independent of whether R-Co has the same shape.

tenants.ex deactivation-status check: restated 'for every HTTP method, not only writes' as being required because 'a read against a deactivated tenant is exactly as much an unauthorized operation as a write is; gating only writes would leave a readable hole in the deactivation guarantee' -- the actual security invariant, not a copy of R-Co's behavior.
